class.name: TerrainDeformer3D
class.brief_description: Non-destructive height brushes (rivers, craters, building plots, road beds) stacked over a heightfield ground.
class.description: Composites a stack of height brushes over the ground's base heights and writes the result into the ground, the edit-layer model of Unreal Engine's Landscape. The deformer remembers the base height of every grid vertex a brush covers, so moving, changing or removing a brush restores the ground it left. Those base heights are saved with the scene, so a ground saved carved can still be restored. Two grounds are supported: - A [code]Terrain3D[/code] node (the Terrain3D addon, installed separately). It is called by name only: the engine does not include or require it. Edited regions are re-uploaded to the height texture array, marked modified so they save, and the addon's collision is rebuilt. - A [CollisionShape3D] holding a [HeightMapShape3D] (not rotated, same scale on X and Z), with an optional [member ground_mesh] that is regenerated from the same heights so it draws and path traces exactly what collides. A brush is any node with a [code]get_carve_brush()[/code] method returning a [Dictionary], or a [code]get_carve_brushes(tile_size)[/code] method returning an [Array] of them (as [code]PhysXRiver3D[/code] does, called with [member brush_tile_size]). Each has [code]rect[/code] ([Rect2], world X and Z), [code]cell_size[/code] ([float]), [code]size[/code] ([Vector2i], samples along X and Z; defaults to [code]rect.size / cell_size[/code]), [code]heights[/code] ([PackedFloat32Array], world Y, row-major with rows along Z), [code]mask[/code] ([PackedFloat32Array], 0 to 1, optional) and [code]mode[/code] ([code]"lower"[/code], [code]"raise"[/code], [code]"flatten"[/code] or [code]"add"[/code]). Samples sit at cell centres: sample [code](i, j)[/code] is at [code]rect.position + (Vector2(i, j) + Vector2(0.5, 0.5)) * cell_size[/code]. [code]"lower"[/code] gives [code]lerp(ground, min(ground, height), mask)[/code], [code]"raise"[/code] the same with [code]max[/code], [code]"flatten"[/code] [code]lerp(ground, height, mask)[/code] and [code]"add"[/code] [code]ground + height * mask[/code]. A NaN height leaves the ground alone. A brush that emits a [code]carve_changed[/code] signal is re-applied automatically when [member auto_apply] is on. [TerrainBrush3D] is a ready-made brush. A brush that measures the ground to place itself (a river following the terrain) should read [method base_height_at] or [method get_base_height], not the carved surface, so re-applying it never digs deeper. Point a [code]PhysXRiver3D[/code]'s [code]base_height_source[/code] at the deformer. Each apply re-uploads the touched Terrain3D regions, so the deformer suits authoring and occasional runtime events (an explosion, a dig), not per-frame deformation.

method.name: add_brush
method.description: Appends [param brush] to the top of the stack.

method.name: apply
method.description: Composites every brush over the base heights and writes the changed vertices into the ground. Returns how many grid vertices changed; [code]0[/code] when nothing did.

method.name: base_height_at
method.description: Same as [method get_base_height], taking world X and Z. This is the call a [code]PhysXRiver3D[/code] makes on its [code]base_height_source[/code].

method.name: clear
method.description: Restores every carved vertex to its base height and forgets the base heights.

method.name: get_backend
method.description: The kind of ground [member terrain] points to.

method.name: get_base_height
method.description: The ground's height at [param global_position] (X and Z) without any brush, interpolated between grid vertices. NaN outside the ground.

method.name: get_carved_vertex_count
method.description: How many grid vertices the deformer keeps a base height for.

method.name: get_height
method.description: The ground's current height at [param global_position] (X and Z), interpolated between grid vertices. NaN outside the ground.

method.name: queue_apply
method.description: Applies once at the end of the frame, however many times it is called.

method.name: remove_brush
method.description: Removes [param brush] from the stack. The ground under it is restored on the next apply.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], applies when the node is ready and whenever a brush emits [code]carve_changed[/code] or the stack changes.
Tile size, in metres, passed to brushes that return their carve as tiles ([code]get_carve_brushes(tile_size)[/code]).
The brush stack, bottom first. Later brushes composite over earlier ones.
For a [HeightMapShape3D] ground: a [MeshInstance3D] whose mesh is rebuilt from the heights after each apply (world-space UVs in metres; the first surface's material is kept).
The ground: a [code]Terrain3D[/code] node, or a [CollisionShape3D] with a [HeightMapShape3D]. Changing it restores the previous ground first.

signal.name: applied
signal.description: Emitted after an apply that changed [param vertices] grid vertices.
